mechanism_narrative: A sustained upward trend in monthly payroll employment growth consistently compresses equity risk premiums by signaling robust labor market conditions, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of months with positive PAYEMS growth, or the Rank IC over 5 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 7.5% and remains below this threshold for two consecutive months, it signals a tightening labor market that boosts corporate hiring and profit growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of triggered instances, or the average return in triggered periods is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in manufacturing production (INDPRO) and payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates a synchronized expansion in industrial output and labor demand, which accelerates corporate earnings growth and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (both INDPRO and PAYEMS rising) fails to produce positive returns in more than 55% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL annualized inflation > 2.5%), a stable or declining federal funds rate signals accommodative monetary policy that supports equity valuations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In high inflation periods (CPIAUCSL annualized inflation > 2.5%), the S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of cases, or the Rank IC for the signal is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained upward trend in housing starts (HOUST) consistently signals strong consumer confidence and residential investment, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of months with rising HOUST, or the Rank IC over 5 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate rises above 0.5% and remains above this level for three consecutive months, it signals a tightening monetary cycle that increases discount rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered instances, or the average return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During manufacturing slowdowns (INDPRO < 95.0), a concurrent decline in housing starts (HOUST < 740.0) signals a broad-based economic contraction that triggers equity sell-offs, driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods of INDPRO < 95.0, the S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of cases when HOUST < 740.0, or the Rank IC for the joint signal is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates robust consumer spending and economic momentum, which accelerates corporate revenue growth and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (both HOUST and RSAFS rising) fails to produce positive returns in more than 55% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.
